witness: ocr_consensus (majority-consensus archaic OCR of the 1582/1609/1610 scans)
modern_anchor: madueke_a (+ sabates_a for the 3 appendix books)

method.approach: content-anchored attestation — anchor on the modern text and corroborate each verse in OCR; NOT from-scratch OCR verse segmentation.
method.fold: shared ocr_sample.skel: long-s / u-v / i-j / vv-w / ligature / silent-e / doubled-letter — bridges archaic PRINT spelling to modern anchor spelling.

product_notes.our-ocr: our FRESH tesseract of the jp2 scans (independent 3rd OCR) — preferred for the stored consensus surface when it attests.
product_notes.djvu: archive.org whole-tome djvu OCR (one file per alias).
product_notes.hocr: archive.org positional hOCR — ocrx_word text extracted.

method.windowing: per book: empirically resolve the best-covering alias per product (mid-chapter probe recall); walk skeleton in canonical order; moving cursor per product; per-verse best_window over a bounded neighbourhood.
method.attest_threshold_rationale: folded TYPE-recall >= 0.5 in the located window. The fold is intentionally lossy (archaic<->modern), and blackletter OCR drops/garbles ~20-40% of tokens, so an exact-match rate is unattainable; 0.5 means a majority of the verse's distinctive modern tokens are corroborated in the print OCR — strong evidence the verse is attested — while rejecting incidental windows. Corroboration DEPTH (how many of the 3 products independently clear 0.5) is the fusion signal.
method.consensus_surface: raw OCR window text of the winning product (prefer our-ocr).
method.determinism: no randomness; identical inputs → identical output.

aggregate.corroboration_depth_note: counts of anchor verses by how many of the 3 OCR products independently cleared the recall threshold. depth 0 = unattested (NOT emitted as a read); depths 1-3 are the emitted reads (depth 3 = all three OCR products corroborate the verse).

caveats: Recall is a CORROBORATION signal, not an exact-match rate: the archaic<->modern fold is lossy and blackletter OCR is noisy, so attestation confirms word-correspondence, not verbatim fidelity.

The stored archaic `surface` is a raw OCR window sliced by folded-token bounds; it may over/under-run the exact verse extent (OCR carries no verse boundaries) and can include adjacent apparatus/marginalia. It is a diplomatic attestation snippet, not a clean verse.
Verses whose modern anchor is short/function-word-heavy are harder to attest (few distinctive tokens) and may fall below threshold despite being present.

our-ocr coverage depends on the background ocr_fulltome job; if it was incomplete at finalisation (see our_ocr_gate/our_ocr_pages_present), affected aliases fall back to djvu+hocr corroboration only (depth capped at 2 there).
